explanations.3: This tells apt-get to not ask interactive questions during installation; it just uses default answers so the build doesn't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.11: After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists to make the image smaller, since we won't need them again.
explanations.14: This pipes a shell script downloaded from the internet directly into sh, which runs it; the empty string and flags after it are arguments passed to that install script.
explanations.20: This uses sed (a text editor) to find the line starting with plugins=(git) and replace it with plugins=(git zsh-syntax-highlighting), adding the new plugin to the list.
explanations.25: The -i flag makes zsh interactive (so it shows prompts), and -l makes it a login shell (so it reads startup files); together they let you actually use the shell interactively.
